methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series G → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.25x) to $75M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Earth AI, founded by Roman Teslyuk, is a Series G infrastructure and logistics company that has raised $20M to date. The valuation analysis is constrained by the absence of comparable public or private peers in the available dataset, limiting triangulation to stage-progression methodology alone.

The stage-progression method applies a 1.25x multiplier to a $75M base value derived from total capital raised, reflecting typical valuation step-ups at the Series G stage. This yields an implied valuation of $94M. The analysis produces a range spanning $80M (low) to $108M (high), with $94M as the median point. This 35% spread around the median reflects methodological bandwidth rather than cross-validation across independent approaches.

The single-method constraint represents a material limitation. Absent comparable company multiples, customer concentration data, or revenue figures, the valuation rests entirely on stage-typical dilution patterns. Key uncertainties include actual burn rate relative to raised capital, revenue traction, and market conditions at the time of next fundraising. A comprehensive valuation would require either identified private peer transactions in infrastructure logistics or public comp analysis at equivalent scales. The $80M–$108M range should be treated as preliminary pending substantive commercial metrics or peer benchmarking.
